**The match is a 2026 FIFA World Cup Round of 32 fixture between the United States (co-hosts, Group D winners) and Bosnia and Herzegovina (Group B third-place team that advanced as one of the best third-placed sides).** All information below draws exclusively from sources published before June 27, 2026, focusing on contextual factors beyond baseline team strength.[[1]](https://www.walb.com/2026/06/26/usa-advances-group-d-world-cup-2026-knockout-stage-takes-shape/)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_FIFA_World_Cup_Group_B)

**Head-to-head history (all friendlies, no major tournament meetings):** The teams have met three times, with the US unbeaten (2 wins, 1 draw). Specific results include:
- August 14, 2013: Bosnia and Herzegovina 3–4 United States.[[3]](https://www.11v11.com/teams/usa/tab/opposingTeams/opposition/Bosnia%20and%20Herzegovina/)
- January 28, 2018: United States 0–0 Bosnia and Herzegovina.[[3]](https://www.11v11.com/teams/usa/tab/opposingTeams/opposition/Bosnia%20and%20Herzegovina/)
- December 18/19, 2021: United States 1–0 Bosnia and Herzegovina.[[3]](https://www.11v11.com/teams/usa/tab/opposingTeams/opposition/Bosnia%20and%20Herzegovina/)[[4]](https://www.sportsmole.co.uk/football/usa/world-cup-2026/head-to-head/usa-vs-bosnia-hvina-head-to-head-record-and-past-meetings_600321.html)

No prior competitive encounters exist, so this is a first-time knockout-stage matchup.[[5]](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/7/1/usa-vs-bosnia-herzegovina-world-cup-round-of-32-prediction-team-lineups)

**Recent form and results (pre-June 27, 2026):** The US topped Group D after wins over Paraguay (4–1 on or around June 12) and Australia (2–0 on or around June 19), followed by a 3–2 loss to Turkey on June 25 (with rotation due to nothing at stake and yellow-card concerns). Wales and Italy) and finishing third in Group B behind Switzerland and Canada (ahead of Qatar on goal difference).[[7]](https://www.uefa.com/european-qualifiers/news/02a6-20d1594a5469-659bdc40eca9-1000--bosnia-and-herzegovina-at-the-world-cup-2026-squad-fixtur/)[[8]](https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/may/28/bosnia-and-herzegovina-world-cup-2026-team-guide)

**Injuries/suspensions (noted in pre-match contexts):** US concerns included Christian Pulisic (calf issue, limited minutes earlier but potentially returning), plus doubts over players like Cristian Roldan (muscle/quadriceps) and others managing minutes after a long club season. Bosnia had no major reported issues in available previews.[[9]](https://sports.yahoo.com/soccer/live/world-cup-live-updates-scores-schedule-results-group-a-group-b-group-c-195336732.html)

**Travel, fatigue, venue, and home advantage:** As co-hosts playing on home soil (likely venues like those in California or the West Coast used in group stage, e.g., areas around Los Angeles/Seattle or similar stadiums), the US benefits from minimal travel, familiar conditions, and strong home crowd support—factors that historically aid hosts in major tournaments. Bosnia faces significant transatlantic travel from Europe, potential jet lag/fatigue in a condensed tournament schedule, and playing away in front of a partisan US crowd. Summer climate in US venues (warm/humid conditions typical for the period) could also factor in, though specific pitch or altitude details for this fixture were not highlighted in pre-June 27 sources.[[10]](https://www.facebook.com/foxsoccer/posts/usas-group-stage-schedule-is-complete-take-a-closer-look-at-who-when-and-where-t/1517253173094931/)

**Other storylines:** Bosnia’s qualification story (playoff heroics under coach Sergej Barbarez, with veteran Edin Džeko as a key figure) adds motivation as underdogs (FIFA ranking gap: US around 15th, Bosnia around 61st). The US, under Mauricio Pochettino, aims for deeper progress than recent World Cups (last knockout win in 2002). No major controversies or unique pitch/altitude issues (e.g., no high-altitude venues noted for this matchup) appear in pre-match coverage.[[6]](https://dknetwork.draftkings.com/2026/07/01/united-states-vs-bosnia-and-herzegovina-prediction-pick-for-wednesday-7-1-26/)[[8]](https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/may/28/bosnia-and-herzegovina-world-cup-2026-team-guide)

These elements—US home advantage and rest advantages, Bosnia’s underdog resilience and travel challenges, plus the limited but favorable US H2H—provide key context beyond raw rankings or squad depth. Sources are primarily official team sites, FIFA/UEFA-related, ESPN, and previews from mid-2026.

factors.impact: Significant positive for the United States, who benefit from being co-hosts with minimal travel, familiar conditions, and strong home crowd support. Bosnia and Herzegovina face considerable transatlantic travel, potential jet lag, and fatigue in a condensed tournament schedule.

The United States demonstrated stronger form, topping their group with two convincing wins and showing strong attacking output. Their rotational loss on June 25 is mitigated. Bosnia and Herzegovina advanced as a best third-place team, suggesting a less dominant group stage performance, despite their playoff heroics to qualify.

The United States holds a favorable, unbeaten record against Bosnia and Herzegovina in three prior friendly encounters (2 wins, 1 draw), providing a psychological edge, even though these were not competitive matches.

The United States has some noted fitness concerns with Christian Pulisic (calf issue, potentially returning) and others managing minutes. Bosnia and Herzegovina report no major injury or suspension issues, slightly mitigating the US advantage, though Pulisic's potential return lessens this impact.

analysis.reasoning: The United States holds a substantial advantage primarily due to their status as co-hosts, providing them with minimal travel, familiar playing conditions, and significant home crowd support in this knockout fixture. This is juxtaposed against Bosnia and Herzegovina's extensive transatlantic travel and likely fatigue. The US also exhibited superior form in the group stage, topping their group with strong attacking performances, while Bosnia advanced as a 'best third-place' team. The historical head-to-head record, though limited to friendlies, also leans in favor of the United States. While there are minor fitness concerns for some US players, they are not expected to fully offset these significant environmental and form-based advantages.
